Why does this matter?
DBMS scope + innovation + measurable research
Reasoning: what is a real entity?

Kept as entities (10): Entity, RelationalRecord, Document, VectorEmbedding, GraphNode, GraphEdge, Query,
QueryPredicate, ExecutionPlan, CostEstimate.

Not entities (software components / processes): Adaptive Planner, Unified Execution Engine, Transaction
Manager. We model the data they read and produce, not the components.

Entity
PK
FKs / key attributes
Purpose
SQL: region, depot, battery health, timestamps, telemetry values — exact relational filtering.

Vector: maintenance reports are natural language ("Battery overheating after prolonged highway operation"); a new
issue is compared against past reports via embeddings.

Graph: Vehicle→Depot, Vehicle→Charging Station, Depot→Charging Station, Vehicle→maintenance history, service
dependencies.

Data
Store
Role

SQL (3NF)
Source of truth for structured transactional data

Report-text embeddings
In-memory HNSW index
Semantic similarity

Logical write: one logical write = relational record + embedding + graph edges → Transaction/Consistency Manager →
consistent state. (Proposed design; exact protocol is part of the implementation plan, not yet finalized.)
